question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is structuring a new Cat II AIF at GIFT IFSC to attract foreign LPs. Which of the following MOST accurately captures the tax advantages available for a Cat I/II AIF set up in IFSC-GIFT compared to an onshore (non-IFSC) Cat I/II AIF?

answer.text: No tax benefit — IFSC funds are taxed identically to onshore AIFs.
IFSC funds pay a flat 5% tax on all income.
IFSC funds are exempt from SEBI AIF Regulations.
IFSC funds enjoy a 100% tax holiday on business income for any 10 consecutive years out of 15 (Section 80LA), and management fees from non-resident LPs are zero-rated / exempt from GST.

explanation.text: The Logic: A Cat I/II AIF located in IFSC-GIFT (regulated by IFSCA under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022) qualifies for Section 80LA of the Income-tax Act — a 100% deduction on prescribed business income for any 10 consecutive years out of 15. In addition, investment-management services rendered by an IFSC-based manager to non-resident LPs are generally zero-rated under GST as exports of services. The Section 115UB / 10(23FBA) pass-through framework for SEBI/IFSCA-registered Cat I/II funds continues to apply. The Trap: Option A ignores the explicit tax-holiday regime; Option B invents a flat 5% rate; Option D is wrong — IFSC funds are regulated by IFSCA (a separate statutory regulator), not exempted from regulation. Note: The XIX-D workbook references IFSC/GIFT structures and IFSC tax benefits in general terms and discusses Section 115UB pass-through for SEBI/IFSCA-registered Cat I/II funds. It does not specifically state the Section 80LA "100% deduction for 10 of 15 years" formulation or the GST zero-rating treatment. The specific Section 80LA wording should be cross-checked against the current Income-tax Act / IFSCA circulars.
